settings.reactivate_min_historic_roas: surface for reactivation if a paused campaign's last active-period ROAS >= 3.0x
settings.budget_reallocation_min_roas_gap: shift budget when one active campaign's ROAS is 1.5x+ another's
settings.note: hard_spend_ceiling_inr is a placeholder — set to roughly 3x trailing-30-day avg daily spend (~₹663/day as of 29 Aug 2026). All fields here are editable directly in the Automation tab (Save button) or by telling Claude.

proposals.title: Launch a retargeting campaign against 30d add-to-cart non-purchasers
proposals.reasoning: Account-level 30d data: 83 add-to-cart events vs 15 purchases — roughly 68 people added to cart in the last 30 days without completing a purchase. Refreshed pixel-level check on 2026-08-29 (trailing 7d window, later same-day re-check) shows the pattern continuing and building: ~60 AddToCart events vs 11 Purchases (up from ~50 AddToCart earlier the same day — Purchase count unchanged at 11). Re-checked again this run (2026-08-29, event-level pull direct from the dataset): 50 AddToCart events vs 11 Purchases over the trailing 7 days — consistent with the same-day earlier reading, Purchase count still unchanged at 11. No retargeting campaign currently exists against this group. Rebuilt 2026-08-29 into a real, executable 4-step chain (previously only had 2 of 4 steps specced, with no real budget/creative/audience-rule values — approving it as originally written would have failed or produced an empty campaign shell). Uses the account's real active pixel ('Shopify Meta Pixel', dataset_id 833131719490535, last fired 2026-08-29) and the real Kage_Sales creative (id 1063318642863205, the account's best-ROAS creative at 4.30x, ad copy 'GRAB THE MOST CLICK-WORTHY SNEAKERS EVER').
proposals.actionSummary: 4-step chain, each step feeding the next real Meta-assigned ID (not guessed): (1) create the WEBSITE pixel audience — AddToCart OR InitiateCheckout in the last 14 days, excluding Purchase; (2) create the campaign (OUTCOME_SALES); (3) create the ad set targeting that new audience, India, Facebook+Instagram, optimizing for purchases, daily_budget 25000 (Meta's minor-currency-unit field — this is ₹250/day, editable via the parameter editor below, same conservative range as A-001's reactivation budget); (4) create the ad reusing the Kage_Sales creative. Every step is created PAUSED — approving this does NOT start spending. You'd review it in Ads Manager and activate manually, or tell Claude to activate once you're satisfied.

proposals.title: Launch a Dynamic Product Ads (DPA) campaign from the connected Shopify catalog
proposals.reasoning: A Shopify product catalog is already connected to this ad account (catalog_id 1149969713295773), but zero DPA/catalog-based campaigns are currently running. Gully Labs (main competitor) runs DCO/catalog ads as part of their active mix; KAI runs none. This is a structural gap, not a performance one. Meta's own Opportunity Score tool has been sliding across the last three runs on 2026-08-29 — 88 → 85 → 81/100 — and re-checked again this run at 81, still flagging Advantage+ catalog ads as a top recommendation (+4 points, 'lower cost per action'); a new offsite-conversion optimization recommendation (+5 points) also surfaced this pass, unrelated to the catalog gap. Catalog health check re-run on 2026-08-29 found the same 3 diagnostic issues, unchanged from the last check: 18 items still marked out-of-stock (must_fix — these won't appear in dynamic ads), 24 items with fewer than 2 images (opportunity), and 1 unmatched content ID between the catalog and pixel (opportunity). Rebuilt 2026-08-29 into a real chain: pulled live catalog product data (81 products total) and found no 'best-seller' field available via the catalog API — that framing was aspirational, not backed by real data, so downgraded to a defensible, real filter instead: in-stock only (availability=in stock), which also structurally avoids advertising the 18 out-of-stock items flagged above.
proposals.actionSummary: 3-step chain, each real: (1) create a product set filtered to in-stock items only; (2) create the campaign (OUTCOME_SALES, PAUSED); (3) create the ad set targeting India broadly with Advantage+ audience (matching the account's existing targeting_automation pattern on Kage_sales_1908), promoted_object pointing at the new product set, daily_budget 25000 (that's ₹250/day), PAUSED. Honest scope limit: the 4th step — the actual dynamic template ad (Meta's product-template creative format, distinct from a static image/video ad) — isn't wired into this automation's creative editor yet, which only builds static ads. Approving this proposal completes steps 1-3; the ad set will sit ready with its promoted_object set, and the final template ad needs one more manual step in Ads Manager (or a follow-up once template-creative support is built).

Its ad set (id 120255351569140159) targets broad interest/behavior segments (Footwear, Sneakers, Street fashion, Frequent Travelers, Engaged Shoppers) with Advantage+ audience expansion on, but the targeting spec still has no excluded_custom_audiences entry — re-checked directly against the live targeting spec on 2026-08-29. A re-check of the account's custom audiences on 2026-08-29 found an existing 'Purchasers 30D' audience (id 120249907176770159, subtype PLATFORM/website pixel-based, delivery_status ACTIVE) that was not previously known — no need to create a new audience, it can be applied directly. proposals.actionSummary: Add the existing 'Purchasers 30D' custom audience (id 120249907176770159) as an excluded audience on Kage_sales_1908's ad set targeting, leaving all other targeting unchanged. No new audience needs to be created.

proposals.title: Exclude WhatsApp placement from Kage_sales_1908
proposals.reasoning: 30d placement breakdown for Kage_sales_1908 (the account's only active sales campaign): the 'whatsapp_marketing_messages' placement spent ₹262.34 on 195 impressions with 0 attributed purchases, at a CPM of ₹1,345.33 — roughly 11x the campaign's android_smartphone CPM (₹117.96) and 8x its iPhone CPM (₹160.51). This same spend shows up identically in the device breakdown as the 'other' impression_device bucket (₹262.34, CPM ₹1,345.33, 0 purchases) — same underlying placement, two views of the same number, not a separate issue. ₹262.34 is ~5.2% of the campaign's ₹5,089.64 30d spend going to a placement with zero conversions at a wildly elevated CPM. By contrast, this campaign's two dominant placements — instagram_reels (₹2,217.98, 1 purchase, 1.13x ROAS) and instagram_stories (₹780.12, 2 purchases, 7.01x ROAS) — are both converting, so this isn't a whole-campaign problem, just this one placement.
proposals.actionSummary: Remove 'whatsapp' from Kage_sales_1908's ad set targeting.publisher_platforms (keep facebook, instagram, audience_network, threads as-is). Note: Meta's targeting spec is inclusion-based (no separate excluded_publisher_platforms field), so this is applied by narrowing the publisher_platforms list rather than adding an exclusion.

proposals.title: Shift Kage_sales_1908 budget weight from 25-34 male toward 35-44 male
proposals.reasoning: 30d age/gender breakdown for Kage_sales_1908 (the account's only active sales campaign): the 25-34 male cell spent ₹2,408.32 (the single largest demo allocation in the campaign) for 1 purchase, ROAS 1.11x — below the campaign's own 30d blended ROAS (1.57x) and well below account average. The 35-44 male cell spent ₹1,118.80, less than half as much, but returned 2 purchases at 4.74x ROAS — over 4x more efficient per rupee spent. Both cells clear a ₹500+ meaningful-spend bar. 18-24 male (₹694.96, 0 purchases) is also underperforming. This is a real, spend-backed efficiency gap within one active campaign, not a cross-objective comparison.
proposals.actionSummary: Corrected 2026-08-29: the original note said 'tighten age_max toward 44', which was backwards — favoring the OLDER 35-44 group means raising the floor (age_min), not lowering the ceiling. Concrete change: raise age_min from the current 21 to 28 (current live targeting confirmed: age_min 21, age_max 65). This is a partial lean, not a hard cutoff — it cuts the weakest 21-27 slice entirely, retains the back half of 25-34 (28-34), and keeps all of 35-44 and everything above. Fully editable in the age-range fields below if you want a different split.

params.note: raise age_min toward 28-30 to lean away from 25-34 male (1.11x ROAS) toward 35-44 male (4.74x ROAS); sample is thin (3 purchases total) so treat as a lean, not a hard cutoff

alerts.title: Geo scaling/suppression can't run yet — Meta doesn't return purchase attribution at region level
alerts.detail: Checked the 30d region breakdown for both active campaigns. Kage_sales_1908 (the only sales campaign) has real spend concentration — Maharashtra ₹1,985.20 (2.16% CTR), Karnataka ₹902.39 (2.33% CTR), Telangana ₹584.60, Delhi ₹543.81 — but every single region row came back with omni_purchase/purchase_roas = null. This isn't a spend-volume problem (Maharashtra alone clears any reasonable meaningful-spend bar); it's the same Meta API limitation already disclosed on the dashboard's Geography tab (purchase attribution isn't returned cross-tabbed with region breakdowns). geo-scaling, geo-suppression, and new-geo-testing can only run on a CTR proxy until that changes, so skipped this run rather than propose budget moves off a proxy metric alone. Re-evaluate once spend is high enough to justify the same CTR-relative-ROAS estimation methodology the dashboard already uses for this tab.

alerts.title: Kage_sales_1908-only hourly pull resolves the earlier account-wide caveat: no actionable dayparting pattern

Original account-wide numbers (₹8,813.10/10 purchases vs ₹9,935.47/5 purchases) were confirmed to be diluted by Kage_TOF as suspected. Downgrading to low severity and not filing a dayparting proposal — will keep watching as purchase volume grows.

alerts.title: Kage_TOF: CTR still soft week-over-week, just under the auto-trigger threshold, not frequency-driven
alerts.detail: Refreshed same-day (2026-08-29, later re-check): Kage_TOF's single active ad CTR is 1.65% over the last 7d vs 2.31% the prior 7d (15-21 Aug) — a 28.6% week-over-week decline, just under the 30% creative-fatigue trigger this run (earlier same-day numbers read 2.35%→1.45%, a 38.3% decline, using a slightly different day-boundary window — both pulls agree directionally: real, sustained softening, not a one-off blip). Still not filed as an executable proposal: no ready replacement creative to rotate in yet (needs the Phase 3 auto-creative-generation pipeline, not yet built).
